mainEntity.name: What does a metal-home interior finish-out include?

acceptedAnswer.text: A metal-home interior finish-out is the complete construction phase that transforms a bare steel shell or barndominium into a fully habitable home. Once the structural steel frame, exterior metal panels, and slab are in place, the finish-out covers interior framing, rough-in plumbing, electrical systems, HVAC installation, insulation, drywall, and final fixtures. A key decision factor during planning is whether to frame interior walls with light-gauge steel studs or traditional lumber, as wood allows easier hanging of heavy cabinets while steel studs eliminate warping and termite concerns in structural integration.
acceptedAnswer.description: A metal-home finish-out turns a raw steel shell into a finished residence by adding interior framing, insulation, plumbing, electrical, HVAC, drywall, and interior fixtures.
